Hey everyone! We're a curious, motivated team passionate about technology, AI, and finding creative solutions to real-world problems. We love brainstorming, learning, and bringing ideas to life!

We're looking for teammates with web development and graphic design skills. No need to be an expert — creativity, enthusiasm, and teamwork matter most!

If you're up for building something exciting and having fun along the way, join us! We promise good vibes and hopefully fewer bugs than features! 🚀
summary:
Devonian is a web-based environmental monitoring platform designed to help users explore and understand environmental changes across Africa, with a focus on wildfire activity. The project provides an interactive dashboard where users can select geographical regions, environmental variables and time periods to analyse environmental trends.

The platform aims to make Earth observation data more accessible and understandable by presenting complex environmental information through a clear, user-friendly interface. By helping users explore patterns of environmental change, it supports greater awareness of wildfire activity and its potential environmental impacts.

This project is important because wildfires and other environmental changes threaten ecosystems, biodiversity and communities across Africa. Making environmental data easier to access and interpret can support informed decision-making, environmental awareness and future research. Our longer-term vision is to incorporate predictive capabilities to help identify areas that may face increased wildfire risk.
details:
Project Details – FIRE & CHANGE: Understanding Wildfire Trends Across Southern Africa

What does the project do and how does it work?

FIRE & CHANGE is a satellite-data-driven environmental monitoring platform that investigates how wildfire activity changes over time across five Southern African countries: Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa. It examines historical data from January 2020 to December 2025 using three key indicators: Burned Area, Fire Radiative Power (FRP) and Active-Fire Detection Frequency.

The system retrieves NASA MODIS satellite observations through Google Earth Engine and the NASA FIRMS API. It then processes the data using geospatial techniques, applies quality-control measures and aggregates observations into monthly and annual datasets. Statistical methods, including the Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope, are used to investigate whether wildfire activity is increasing or decreasing and to estimate the magnitude of observed changes.

The processed information is made accessible through an interactive web platform, allowing users to explore environmental indicators, compare countries and investigate trends over time.

What are the benefits and intended impact?

Wildfires can significantly affect ecosystems, biodiversity, agricultural land and communities. Our platform helps transform large and complex satellite datasets into meaningful environmental indicators and statistical findings.

Its intended impact is to improve awareness and understanding of wildfire patterns across Southern Africa, support environmental research and make Earth observation data more accessible to students, researchers and environmental organisations. By identifying measurable changes in wildfire activity, the system can contribute to more informed environmental monitoring and decision-making.

What tools and technologies were used?

The project combines several technologies:

  • NASA MODIS MCD64A1 Collection 6.1: Used for monthly burned-area observations.
  • NASA FIRMS API: Used to retrieve active-fire observations from MODIS Terra and Aqua.
  • Google Earth Engine: Used to access and process satellite data.
  • Python: Used for data processing, geospatial analysis and statistical calculations.
  • FastAPI: Used to develop the backend and REST API.
  • Pydantic: Used for API data validation and schemas.
  • React and TypeScript: Used to develop the interactive frontend.
  • Vite: Used as the frontend development and build tool.
  • Git and GitHub: Used for version control and team collaboration.

How is the project creative and innovative?

The creativity of our project lies in combining satellite observations, geospatial processing and statistical analysis into one integrated platform. Instead of simply displaying the locations of detected fires, it investigates whether wildfire activity is changing over time, the direction and magnitude of those changes, and whether there is statistical evidence supporting the observed trends.

Using three complementary indicators provides a broader understanding of wildfire activity. The interactive platform also allows users to explore different countries and time periods without needing to work directly with raw satellite datasets.

What factors did the team consider?

Our team considered data accuracy, satellite observation limitations, missing observations, geographical differences and the reliability of statistical results. We also considered the importance of distinguishing active-fire satellite detections from unique wildfire incidents, since multiple satellite detections do not necessarily represent separate fires.

The study's six-year period is relatively short for establishing long-term environmental trends. Seasonal patterns, autocorrelation and missing observations must also be considered when interpreting results. These limitations are documented to encourage responsible interpretation of the findings.

Our longer-term vision includes incorporating additional satellite sources, extending the historical analysis period, improving spatial visualisation and making the platform available to a wider audience.
